To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the prevalence of lipodystrophy in HIV-infected patients on HAART in the Netherlands is high, that the syndrome is associated with dyslipidaemia, and that dyslipidaemia is associated with steroid hormone alterations.

(i) the prevalence of HIV-associated dyslipidemia and lipodystrophy is high in HIV-infected patients, and is associated with the use of protease inhibitors; and (ii) HIV-associated dyslipidaemia is associated with a higher risk of cardiovascular disease.

the use of a novel method for the detection of lipodystrophy in patients with HIV infection is associated with the presence of metabolic disorders and hormonal alterations, and that the use of this method is associated with the use of antiretrovirus.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel class of materials for the treatment of HIV/AIDS and related disorders, including lipodystrophy.
the development and validation of a new clinical score to define lipodystrophy syndrome in HIV-infected patients on HAART.
the study of the relationship between the lipodystrophy syndrome, the dyslipidaemia syndrome and the hormonal alterations that occur in men on HAART, in the context of HIV infection.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the lipodystrophy syndrome in HIV-infected patients on HAART is multifactorial and that there is no single factor responsible for its occurrence.
the most common cause of lipodystrophy is the result of the HAART regimen, but that the syndrome is not caused by a single agent.
